notes: Every eval runs a real `claude -p` session with the plugin loaded, against a throwaway git repo, with a tracing shim in front of the real Grok Build CLI. Assertions grade what Claude did (routing, forwarder discipline, review discipline) and the exact argv the plugin handed to Grok.

evals.name: Natural-language delegation reaches Grok write-capable
evals.prompt: the ttl test in test/cache.test.mjs is failing and i can't spot why. get grok to fix it
evals.expected_output: Claude spawns grok:grok-rescue, which makes exactly one write-capable `task` call and returns Grok's stdout verbatim. Grok fixes the expiresAt bug.

assertions.text: Spawns the grok:grok-rescue subagent instead of handling it in the main thread
The Grok run starts instead of dying on a CLI/sandbox rejection
assertions.pattern: refusing to start|could not apply the '|sandbox could not be applied|sandbox profile '[^']*' not found

assertions.text: Invokes the Grok CLI exactly once
Runs Grok write-capable by default (edit tools not blocked) for a fix request
Leaves the model unset when the user did not ask for one
Leaves reasoning effort unset when the user did not ask for one
Rescue subagent uses at most one tool call, and only Bash
Rescue subagent never reads, greps, or edits the repository itself
Final response carries the companion's Grok output through to the user
The failing TTL test passes afterwards

evals.name: Read-only diagnosis request does not get write access
evals.prompt: ask grok to investigate why the ttl test fails and explain the root cause. diagnose only, do not change any code
evals.expected_output: Claude routes to grok:grok-rescue, which runs Grok WITHOUT --always-approve. No file on disk changes.

assertions.text: Spawns the grok:grok-rescue subagent
The Grok run starts instead of dying on a CLI/sandbox rejection
assertions.pattern: refusing to start|could not apply the '|sandbox could not be applied|sandbox profile '[^']*' not found

assertions.text: Invokes the Grok CLI exactly once
Blocks Grok's edit tools when the user asked for diagnosis only
Leaves every file in the repository untouched
Rescue subagent never reads, greps, or edits the repository itself

evals.name: Rescue flags map onto the right Grok CLI arguments
evals.prompt: /grok:rescue --model build --effort medium --fresh fix the ttl expiry bug in src/cache.js
evals.expected_output: Grok is invoked with `-m grok-4.5 --effort medium --sandbox workspace`, no --resume, and the routing flags are stripped from the natural-language task text.

assertions.text: Maps the `build` alias onto the concrete grok-4.5 model id
The Grok run starts instead of dying on a CLI/sandbox rejection
assertions.pattern: refusing to start|could not apply the '|sandbox could not be applied|sandbox profile '[^']*' not found

assertions.text: Passes `--effort medium` through to the Grok CLI
Honours --fresh by not resuming a prior session
Runs Grok write-capable for an explicit fix request
Routing flags do not leak into the natural-language prompt sent to Grok
Invokes the Grok CLI exactly once

evals.name: Review presents findings and stops without fixing
evals.expected_output: Grok reviews the uncommitted change, Claude relays the findings, and no file is touched. The expiresAt bug should appear in the findings.

assertions.text: Invokes the Grok CLI exactly once
The Grok run starts instead of dying on a CLI/sandbox rejection
assertions.pattern: refusing to start|could not apply the '|sandbox could not be applied|sandbox profile '[^']*' not found

assertions.text: Blocks Grok's edit tools for a review
Claude never invokes a file-editing tool during or after the review
Leaves every file in the repository untouched
Grok's review identifies the TTL/expiresAt defect
Those findings actually appear in the user-visible response, not just in the tool result

evals.name: Trivial local edits are not handed off to Grok
evals.prompt: add a short JSDoc comment above the get() method in src/cache.js explaining what it returns
evals.expected_output: Claude does this itself. Grok is never invoked and the rescue subagent is never spawned.

assertions.text: Never invokes the Grok CLI for a task the main thread can finish
Never spawns the grok:grok-rescue subagent
Claude edits src/cache.js itself

evals.name: Natural-language review request reaches Grok or points at the command
evals.prompt: can grok look over my uncommitted changes and tell me if anything looks wrong?
evals.expected_output: Because /grok:review sets disable-model-invocation, Claude cannot call it directly. Either it routes the review through the rescue subagent, or it tells the user to run /grok:review. What it must not do is silently review the code itself.

assertions.text: Either Grok actually runs, or the user is pointed at /grok:review
Leaves every file in the repository untouched
Claude never invokes a file-editing tool for a review request
